title: Cohort-aware Progressive Swap Controller for Model Version Lifecycle
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Introduces cohort-aware progressive swap controller for model version lifecycle. Enables safe, dependency-aware swaps across cohorts with automated rollback and console integration. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Context and motivation: Rolling model versions safely at scale requires more than traffic splitting — it requires cohort-based swaps that respect downstream dependencies, per-cohort evaluation windows, and automated rollback when service-level guards fail. This PR introduces the Cohort-aware Progressive Swap Controller (CPSC), a controller in the rollout orchestration layer that performs swap-style rollouts by progressing model versions cohort-by-cohort rather than sample-level splits.

Goals: reduce exposure of regressions, preserve cold-start isolation, enable dependency-aware health checks (datastore schema, adapter compatibility), and provide deterministic swap semantics for auditability.

High-level design:
- Cohorts are lightweight tagged slices of users (by tenant, georegion, or feature flag).
- Swap phases: prepare (warm KV caches, prefetch embeddings), probe (low volume sanity queries), verify (metrics evaluation), promote (full cohort swap), and finalize (rotate canaries out).
- Safety gates: latency p99, error_rate, model-output-divergence against baseline (approx-match), and dependency liveness.
- Rollback: automated hysteresis back-off + dependency trust graph to determine rollback scope (single cohort vs global).
- Integrations: Redwood Model Registry (version pinning), Console UI hooks for cohort rollout visualization, and Linear/Jira links.

Review conversation:
- Jamal Ortega (reviewer): "Controller looks sane but the probe/promote timeouts seem conservative for low-latency tenants. Can we make timeouts configurable per-cohort?"
- Author (Priya): "Agree; added per-cohort timeout override with sensible defaults and inheritance from organization policy. See cohortrollout_types.go lines 78-96."
- Hannah Li (SRE): "How does this interact with autoscaler decisioning? If a cohort gets promoted and consumes more GPU, will dedicated pools trigger scale-up?"
- Author: "We emit rollout-weight and anticipated qps signal to the autoscaler; autoscaler rules updated in charts/ to acknowledge rollout signals. Added integration test to validate scale-up within 2 minutes in canary env."
- Evan Park (perf): "We should validate p99 regressions with the same input distribution; unit tests use synthetic inputs — add a perf harness run."
- Author: "Added perf baseline run and recorded results in tests/perf/README. Perf CI step added as optional gating check."

Change requests and follow-ups:
- Requested: make dependency checks extensible (plugin interface) — implemented.
- Requested: add audit trail events for each swap decision — implemented via rollout trace events.

- Perf-smoke: non-blocking but added perf baseline artifact

Observability and operational notes:
- Emitted metrics: rollout_cohort_latency_p99, rollout_cohort_error_rate, rollout_cohort_divergence_score, rollout_promote_duration

- Backwards compatibility: CohortRollout CRD marked alpha; if controller not installed, legacy traffic-split semantics unchanged.

Limitations and future work:
- Currently tag-based cohorts only; next step is user-segmentation by behavior and adaptive cohort sizing
- Add automated A/B metric-driven multi-variant experiments that wire into Optimize
- Add rate-limited shadow traffic tests for latent failure modes
